function.name: file_write_full
function.description: file_write_full is used to write the given content to the given file. The existing content of the file will be replaced with the given content.

file_name.description: The name of the file where the content will be written.

content.description: The content that will be written to the file.

function.name: file_read_full
function.description: file_read_full is used to read the full contents of the file with the given name. This function should not be used for large files, which should be read in smaller portions using the file_read_lines function. To determine the size of the file use the file_size_bytes function.

file_name.description: The name of the file to read.

function.name: file_read_lines
function.description: file_read_lines is used to read specific lines from a file and is useful for reading portions of a large file. Use the file_size_lines function to determine the number of lines in a file.

file_name.description: The name of the file to read.

start_line.description: The line at which to start reading.

stop_line.description: The line at which to stop reading.

function.name: file_size_bytes
function.description: file_size_bytes is used to determine the size of a file in bytes.

file_name.description: The name of the file to read.

function.name: file_size_lines
function.description: file_size_lines is used to determine the number of lines in a file.

file_name.description: The name of the file to read.

function.name: file_find_glob
function.description: file_find_glob is used to find files and directories using glob patterns.

glob.description: The glob pattern to use to find a file or directory.

function.name: file_edit
function.description: file_edit replaces old_string with new_string in a file, without needing to rewrite the whole file. Unless replace_all is set, old_string must match exactly one place in the file, so include enough surrounding lines or context to make it unique — if it matches more than once, the call fails and tells you how many times it matched instead of guessing which one you meant.

file_name.description: The name of the file to edit.

old_string.description: The exact text to find and replace. Must match the file's content exactly, including whitespace.

new_string.description: The text to replace old_string with.

replace_all.description: If true, replace every occurrence of old_string instead of requiring exactly one match. Defaults to false.

function.name: file_delete
function.description: file_delete removes a single file. It refuses to delete a directory.

file_name.description: The name of the file to delete.

function.name: file_move
function.description: file_move moves or renames a file or directory from source to destination. It does not create destination's parent directory — use dir_create first if it doesn't exist yet.

source.description: The current path of the file or directory.

destination.description: The new path for the file or directory.

function.name: dir_create
function.description: dir_create creates a directory, along with any missing parent directories (like "mkdir -p"). It is not an error if the directory already exists.

function.name: dir_list
function.description: dir_list lists the immediate contents of a directory (not recursive — use file_find_glob or grep_files to search recursively), one entry per line as "type<TAB>size<TAB>name".

path.description: The directory to list. Defaults to the current directory if omitted.

function.name: grep_files
function.description: grep_files searches files under a directory tree for lines matching a regular expression, returning "file:line: text" per match. Use this to find where something is used or defined across a codebase, instead of reading whole files one at a time. .git directories are always skipped.

pattern.description: A regular expression to search for (RE2 syntax, the same as Go's regexp package).

path.description: The directory to search recursively. Defaults to the current directory if omitted.

glob.description: Restrict the search to files whose name matches this glob pattern, e.g. "*.go". Searches all files if omitted.

max_results.description: Maximum number of matches to return. Defaults to 200 if omitted.
